title: Goodwill on Bank Deposit Incorrect-Amount Make-Good Credits for Slow Decisions
content:
The make-good credit for a Bank Deposit incorrect amount carries a goodwill percentage that follows how long Paloma took to decide the incorrect-amount notice; the goodwill percentage raises the shortfall value.

## How the time is measured

The goodwill percentage follows how long Paloma took to decide, counted in calendar days from the incorrect-amount notice to the decision finding the error on that notice. Both dates are read from the transfer's case file: the date of the incorrect-amount notice, and the date of the decision recording "error found" on it.

## Clause

A decision at least 14 calendar days after the notice accrues 3 percent for every whole week between the notice and the decision, never more than a cap of 12 percent; a decision at least 7 but fewer than 14 calendar days after the notice takes a flat 4 percent; a quicker decision is not affected by this rule. A whole week is each complete run of seven days in the days counted.

## Schedule

| Calendar days from notice to decision | Whole weeks | Goodwill percentage |
|---|---|---|
| 6 or fewer | — | not affected |
| 7 to 13 | — | 4 percent (flat) |
| 14 to 20 | 2 | 6 percent |
| 21 to 27 | 3 | 9 percent |
| 28 to 34 | 4 | 12 percent |
| 35 or more | 5 or more | 12 percent (the cap) |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- 13 days: fewer than 14, at least 7, so a flat 4 percent.
- 14 days: two whole weeks at 3 percent each, so 6 percent.
- 20 days: still two whole weeks, so 6 percent.
- 35 days: five whole weeks would give 15 percent, held at the 12 percent cap.
